hook_text: At night the ramp carries three tonnes of its own concrete. At the bell it carries something far worse: three hundred running learners.
clip_script: Static load: weight that stays still. The slab itself, three tonnes, pressing down forever. A parked wheelchair. Predictable, easy. Dynamic load: it moves, hits or repeats. The crowd at the bell. A learner jumping two steps lands with three or four times their weight. A crowd leaning sideways on the rail. Ten thousand footsteps a term growing a hairline crack. Even load: spread out, everyone shares. Uneven load: a wheelchair's four hard wheels, a trolley on the kerb, a crowd bunched at one end tipping a landing. Over a washed-out hollow, one wheel can crack a slab a crowd could not. So: thicker treads, mesh inside, posts set deep, rails built for a sideways push.
visual_style: Whiteboard ramp and stairs: a steady downward arrow for dead load, then a flurry of arrows for the crowd, a single large arrow for a jump; four small wheel points on a slab with a hollow beneath.
mood: Dramatic contrast between quiet and rush; engineer's respect for forces.
pacing: Night versus bell, impact, repetition, spread versus bunched, the design answer.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and spot one dynamic and one point load on your way home.
